traits.hypanthium.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 252, 505: Simpson calls the flowers epigynous. Simpson p. 505 defines hypogynous and epigynous as flowers without a hypanthium.

traits.note: Hutchinson (vol. 2, 2nd ed., 1959), family 369 Zingiberaceae: perennial herbs, usually aromatic, with creeping tuberous rhizomes; leaves in two ranks, sheathing at the base, the blade large with many close parallel veins running obliquely from the midrib; flowers mostly bisexual, irregular or lopsided; perianth of 6 in two whorls, the outer calyx-like, the inner petal-like; one fertile stamen, often with petal-like staminodes; ovary inferior, of 3 (rarely 2) cells; fruit fleshy and staying shut, or a capsule opening in three.

traits.leaf_habit.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Zingiberaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Costaceae: how long the leaves last (character 37), coded evergreen. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.rosette.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Zingiberaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Costaceae: whether the leaves gather in rosettes (character 22), coded usually no rosette, sometimes a basal rosette. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.life_span.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data, items edited May 2026), family Zingiberaceae as that work draws it, there coded together with Costaceae: the herbs' life form (character 21), coded perennial. Read from the coded states by script (spec-rework/b1/delta/mapdelta.py with character 21 added); states the authors do not qualify, side by side, read as often.

traits.zygomorphy.note: Watson and Dallwitz, The Families of Flowering Plants (DELTA data), family Zingiberaceae with Costaceae: flowers very irregular, the corolla's median member largest, the stamens reduced to one fertile and the rest joined in a showy lip. That lip below two smaller petals is drawn as an orchid's lip is: zygomorphy labellate.

traits.leaf_division.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 249, 252, family Zingiberaceae: leaf division simple; read as "simple".

traits.leaf_venation.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 249, 252, family Zingiberaceae: leaf venation penni-parallel; read as "pinnate".

traits.sexual_system.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 249, 252, family Zingiberaceae: sexual system hermaphrodite; read as "hermaphrodite".

traits.axis_growth.note: Simpson, Plant Systematics (2019) p. 249, 252, family Zingiberaceae: axis growth sympodial; read as "sympodial".
